environment: two taps across a morpheme boundary (stem-final ɾV + suffix in ɾ-)
notes: Tap nasalization: 'two adjacent taps are pronounced as a long nasal, /ɾɾ/ → [n:]' (mɣɐɾɨ̆-ɾi ðoŋosaɾŏ → [mɣɐn:i ðoŋosaɾŏ] 'a man from Sonsorol'); the ɾ of the suffix is not kept. They suggest the nasal may be 'the realization of a geminate rhotic tap' (p. 40). Van den Berg (2014: 20) gives [n].
Written ɣɬ, 'voiced lateral-fricativised velar': 'because of the fricativisation, at certain points, it comes out as devoiced' (p. 37). The devoiced value is written here with a ring below.

Low vowel raising and fronting: 'a single low vowel, /ɐ/, is fronted and raised to /ɛ/ between two high unrounded vowels' (imɣɐ̆-ɾi → [imɣɛɾi] 'house of', but i:mɣɐ̆-ɾ → [imɣɐɾ] 'his house') (pp. 41-42).

environment: in the 1sg object suffix -ai after a stem-final ɐ
notes: 'The first vowel of the first person singular object marker suffix /-ai/ ... becomes [ɛ] after a stem-final /ɐ/', with glide epenthesis: xɐ-fɐðɐ̆-ai → [xɐfɐðɐjɛi] 'to give birth to me' (pp. 38-39).
Vowel rounding: 'an unrounded vowel /i/, /ɪ/, /ɛ/, /ɐ/ becomes rounded when followed by a rounded vowel' (bɣi-wow → [bɣuwou] 'to go out') (p. 42).

environment: before a rounded vowel (a final ʉ resurfacing before a suffix)
notes: Vowel rounding: ʝɐɾɨðʉ̆ 'ghost' + -ɾi → [ʝɐɾuðʉɾi] 'ghost of', where the suffix brings back the devoiced final ʉ (p. 42).
